args.goal: Find one Canadian ecommerce agency or implementation partner with a current first-party invitation for subcontractors or specialists that explicitly covers a discrete merchant-feed or catalogue migration QA task. Start with the full mission history and saved partner research. Reuse equivalent work and exclude item 4, previously assessed prospects without changed evidence, unsolicited contact and generic partnership pages. Use at most three first-party public captures on a concrete fit, counting refusals. Confirm the invitation, scope, response route and any stated vendor conditions. If the agency publishes a relevant acceptance rule, run the existing merchant controls on fictional passing and failing rows tied to that rule, then produce a copy-ready operator response with scoped output, AI disclosure, provisional CAD quote and any payment or eligibility conditions still open. If no current invitation qualifies, record the exact source coverage and the evidence that would reopen this route. Save and read back the evidence under products/services/catalogue-invited-agency-pilot/ and close under a valid lease with a lesson. No submission, external contact, account creation, spending or deployment. Any subsequent public deployment goes through the host's independent exact-digest review. Track invitation, submission, accepted order, delivery and verified settlement separately.

description: Treasury is unfunded and reports CAD 0 in verified revenue. The latest feedback has no classified commercial signal and five unclassified sources, so demand remains unknown. The UK screen covered 25 notices and found quality-assurance criteria within larger contracts. A current notice offering a separately priced remote deliverable would reopen that route. The next experiment focuses on reachable buyers for the tested catalogue service and reuses the existing fulfilment work. The completed NLnet follow-up will be read to establish whether an application is actionable.
